questions.question: You’re at a party and someone spills their drink on your new jacket. What would be the most appropriate way to respond if you want to apologise sincerely and offer to help clean it up?
options: Don’t worry about it. It’s not my fault!
Oh no, that’s terrible! I’ll get some paper towels right away.
I’m sure you’ll find it easily. You must have been distracted.
You’re lucky it’s not worse. I’ll take care of it later.
questions.answer: Oh no, that’s terrible! I’ll get some paper towels right away.

questions.question: Your colleague suggests, ‘Let’s meet tomorrow at 3 PM to finalise the project plan.’ How would you politely respond if you’re unable to attend?
options: That’s a great idea! I’ll definitely make it tomorrow.
I’m sorry, but I can’t make it tomorrow—my schedule’s full.
Tomorrow’s fine with me, but we should meet earlier to save time.
I’ll bring the plan tomorrow, but I won’t be there in person.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I can’t make it tomorrow—my schedule’s full.

questions.question: In a formal meeting, someone says, ‘I believe we should reconsider the budget allocation for this quarter.’ What is the most appropriate way to agree with their suggestion while also suggesting a different approach?
options: That’s a good point. I think we should keep the budget the same.
I agree, but perhaps we could allocate more funds to marketing first.
You’re wrong; the budget should stay unchanged.
That’s a bad idea. We need to cut expenses elsewhere.
questions.answer: I agree, but perhaps we could allocate more funds to marketing first.

questions.question: Your friend asks, ‘Did you enjoy the concert last night?’ What would be the most natural way to politely disagree while still expressing appreciation?
options: No, it was terrible—I didn’t enjoy it at all.
I loved it! It was amazing, but I didn’t get to see my favourite band.
I’m not sure. It was okay, but I didn’t feel comfortable there.
I didn’t go, but I heard it was great—maybe you should try it again.
questions.answer: I loved it! It was amazing, but I didn’t get to see my favourite band.

questions.question: A stranger in a café asks, ‘Would you mind if I sit here?’ What is the most appropriate way to respond if you are already seated and want to politely decline?
options: No, go ahead—I’ll sit over there.
I’m sorry, but I’m already seated here. Maybe you’d prefer that table?
That’s fine, but you should sit closer to the window.
I don’t mind. You can sit here if you like.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I’m already seated here. Maybe you’d prefer that table?
